subject: t/op batch-2 survey: 5 OK, 7 DIFF — cproto.t is ONE family (183 rows, prototype("CORE::…")), defer.t is an unimplemented feature, 2 crashers
description:
MEASURED s319 (second batch of t/op originals, after batch 1 gave 10 OK / 2 DIFF).
Recorded so nobody re-measures.  None of these were triaged further.

FULLY OK (5): op/alarm.t 5/0, op/arith2.t 9/0, op/assignwarn.t 116/0,
op/auto.t 47/0, op/die_exit.t 17/0.

DIFF (7), most promising first:

 * op/catch.t 10/2 — the 2 rows are UNITCHECK-in-string-eval, task #174.
 * op/cproto.t 71/183 — **ONE FAMILY**: the file calls prototype("CORE::foo")
   for every core builtin and the failing rows are one per builtin (write,
   warn, wantarray, waitpid, wait, vec, …).  So it is core-builtin PROTOTYPE
   INTROSPECTION, not 183 separate bugs.  Likely a single table of core
   prototypes; check first whether perl's answers are worth hard-coding or
   whether this is principle-9-adjacent (a program that asks for a core
   prototype is doing introspection, not running).  183 rows is the second
   biggest block in t/op after cmpchain's 274.
 * op/attrproto.t 17/28 — attribute + prototype interaction.
 * op/anonsub.t 1/5 (perl 14/1) — PCL produces only 1 ok, so it stops early.
 * op/defer.t 0/0, `undef-fn:main::pl-defer` — the `defer { }` block (perl
   5.36 feature) is simply not implemented, so the file produces NO TAP.
   Either implement or bless; it is a clean, self-contained feature.
 * op/anonconst.t 0/1 CRASH — "Undefined subroutine &main:: called at (eval N)"
   — an EMPTY sub name in a crash message, which smells like a real parse bug
   worth its own probe.
 * op/decl-refs.t 187/197 CRASH — declared references (`my \$x`, perl 5.26
   feature).  Half the file passes then it dies.

METHOD NOTE: batch measurement (12 files, --jobs 3, ~3 min) then classifying by
row-count and description SHAPE is much cheaper than per-file investigation.
`cut -f4- | sed 's/[0-9]\+/N/g' | sort | uniq -c` collapses a faillog into its
families in one line — that is how cmpchain's 274 and cproto's 183 were each
identified as a single cause.

DO NOT run op/list.t or op/pack.t in any batch (task #160: op/list.t OOMs the
whole run).
